acceptance: The run-timeout cleanup warning matches each platform's verification state in the owner's chosen wording.
context: Filed 2026-11-25 at the close of the run-timeout effort (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120, done). Evidence read that day; re-read code, docs and run folders before acting.
description:
## Problem
`REMOTE_CLEANUP_WARNING` in `benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py` (owner's verbatim text from run-timeout-plan-20261120) says: "A run time limit is set. If the run times out, BenchBox will try to cancel the work it started on {platform}. This cleanup has not been checked against the live service, so work may keep running and billing." It printed on the 2026-11-25 BigQuery run, although BigQuery cleanup has now been checked live (docs/operations/run-safety.md (capability table) says so). The warning was left unchanged because it is the owner's wording.

## Change
Ask the owner for the wording, then implement it: either one text per platform group (live-checked vs stub-only, chosen from a per-platform flag such as a manifest capability), or one revised text for all.

## Decision gates
- STOP and ask the owner (choice dialog) for the exact text(s); quote them verbatim on this item and in code.
- Do not mark a platform live-checked without evidence (see run-timeout-cleanup-live-check-more-platforms-20261125).

## Verification rubric
Pass: tests in `tests/unit/cli/test_run_timeout_remote_cleanup.py` and the MCP warning path show the chosen text for BigQuery and for a stub-only platform, failing before; `docs/operations/run-safety.md` (the quoted warning) updated in the same pull request; benchbox-site `docs/reference/cli/run.md` updated in a pull request into `next`; `make platform-manifest-check` (if a manifest flag is added) and `make pr-preflight` exit 0.
Fail: a warning or doc that claims a live check without evidence, or any copy of the old text left.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
